rows.config: complement-pair 6e half top2 aux=0.0001 unfreeze moe-norm 5k
rows.notes: Only unfreezes layer12-23 mlp_norm around the MoE blocks. Under the unified reevaluation protocol it is effectively tied with the fixed-norm aux=0.0001 5K baseline: slightly worse at PPL@64 and slightly better at PPL@1024.

rows.config: complement-pair 6e half top2 aux=0.0001 learnable pair-scale 5k
rows.notes: Adds 36 positive log-scale parameters for per-layer/per-pair output scaling. Learned scales drift below 2.0 (mean 1.819, min 1.721, max 1.890) but remain slightly worse than the fixed-scale aux=0.0001 5K baseline under the unified reevaluation protocol.

Allows all 15 top-2 pairs but scores them with a fixed coverage-penalty lambda=2.0. In practice it collapses back to the three strict complement pairs, so routing freedom does not translate into better PPL.

Uses a strict complement base pair plus one extra free expert with free_expert_scale=0.5, raising active width to 1.5I. It is clearly better than the standard 6E 5K baseline, but still behind the best scratch 20K complement-pair run.
full-width top-1 active-path-fair variant trained from scratch to 20k; healthy load balance but expert similarity remains high
First scratch 20K complement-pair run; strong specialization and clear gains over non-MoE, though later aux=0.0001 20K improves further.
Scratch 20K extension of the best 5K aux=0.0001 setting; best complement-pair result so far, beating the earlier aux=0.005 20K run on both eval conventions.

Continue from the best aux=0.0001 20K checkpoint with model-weight-only init, keep MoE lr=1e-4, and unfreeze the full transformer backbone at lr=1e-5 while keeping embeddings and lm_head frozen. Improves PPL@1024 by about 0.007 over the base 20K checkpoint.
Continue from the same best 20K checkpoint, but only unfreeze layer12-23 attn and norm parameters at lr=1e-5. Slightly improves PPL@1024 over the base 20K checkpoint, but the gain is extremely small.

Initialized from the dense MMfreeLM-370M checkpoint, upcycled into 6E complement-pair MoE, and jointly trained MoE plus layer12-23 local backbone for 20K steps. Training was stable and load balance stayed nearly uniform, but final PPL@1024 is clearly worse than the best scratch aux=0.0001 20K complement-pair run.

rows.config: moe8e half top2 random extreme local-backbone-ft 40k

rows.config: complement-pair 6e half top3 pair+free scale=0.50 aux=0.0001 20k
rows.notes: 20K pair-plus-free with free_expert_scale=0.50 remains stable and clearly better than strict 5K baselines, but still trails the best 6E complement scratch-20K mainline at PPL@1024.

Iso-area shared-residual MoE with strict parameter fairness (delta -491,700 params), resolved shared width 2288 and active width ratio 0.858x dense. Training and formal eval complete, but perplexity is far worse than the non-MoE baseline and the complement-pair mainline; alpha=0.10 is not a promising setting.

Same iso-area shared-residual design but residual_scale_init=0.25. Slightly better than alpha=0.10 on both eval conventions, but still dramatically underperforms the dense baseline and all viable 6E complement routes despite meeting strict parameter-fairness constraints.

rows.init: exact full shared dense copy + random_ternary_matched residual experts
rows.notes: Rerun after fixing shared-copy norm and dtype bugs. exact full-width shared path (2816) plus 4x64 top1 residual, moe_only freeze. Lands essentially on top of the dense baseline, indicating the previous worse full-shared result was implementation contamination rather than structural failure.

rows.init: exact full shared dense copy + random_ternary_matched residual experts
rows.notes: Rerun after the shared-copy bugfix. exact full-width shared path plus 8x32 top2 residual, moe_only freeze. Slightly better than the 4x64 top1 variant and marginally better than the dense baseline on formal 1024-sample eval.

rows.init: exact full shared dense copy + random_ternary_matched residual experts
rows.notes: Rerun after the shared-copy bugfix. exact full-width shared path plus 4x64 top1 residual, local_backbone_ft freeze. Essentially tied with the moe_only twin and the dense baseline, so local backbone unfreezing adds very little in the full-shared setting.

rows.init: exact full shared dense copy + random_ternary_matched residual experts
rows.notes: Best clean full-shared rerun after fixing the shared-copy bug. exact full-width shared path plus 8x32 top2 residual, local_backbone_ft freeze. Slightly outperforms the dense baseline and all other full-shared controls, showing that a small residual branch can help once the shared path is kept exact.

rows.config: shared-residual topchannel 2288 + 4x128 top1 discard alpha=0.25 local-backbone-ft 5k
rows.notes: Clean rerun after fixing the shared-copy bug. Strict-parameter-fair topchannel shared-residual with 4x128 top1 discarded-channel residuals remains very weak; despite healthy load balance it is far worse than both the dense baseline and the full-shared controls.

rows.config: shared-residual topchannel 2288 + 4x128 top1 discard alpha=0.25 moe-only 5k
rows.notes: Clean rerun after the shared-copy bugfix. The moe_only twin is essentially tied with the local_backbone_ft version, so local backbone training does not rescue the topchannel 2288 + 4x128 discarded-residual design.

rows.config: shared-residual topchannel 2288 + 8x64 top2 discard alpha=0.25 local-backbone-ft 5k
rows.notes: Clean rerun after the shared-copy bugfix. 8x64 top2 is slightly better than 4x128 top1 on PPL, but router entropy drops and sparse load imbalance rises sharply (~0.44), so the gain comes with clearly unhealthy residual routing.

rows.config: shared-residual topchannel 2288 + 8x64 top2 discard alpha=0.25 moe-only 5k
rows.notes: Clean rerun after the shared-copy bugfix. The moe_only twin is almost identical to local_backbone_ft, reinforcing that the main failure is structural: compressing shared width to 2288 is too damaging, and discarded residual experts do not compensate enough.

rows.notes: Eval-only diagnostic built directly from the dense checkpoint using the same resolved shared width 2288, with sparse residual disabled. It is worse than the trained 4x128 top1 shared-residual run by about 0.437 PPL, which means the residual branch is not the primary cause of failure; the compressed shared path is already badly damaged on its own.

rows.config: diagnostic shared-only-from-dense 2288 for 4x128 top1 discard moe-only
rows.init: dense checkpoint -> shared-only dense-top-channel 2288, no router, no sparse experts
rows.notes: Eval-only diagnostic matching the moe_only 4x128 source experiment. Again, shared-only 2288 from dense is clearly worse than the trained shared-residual counterpart, so sparse residuals are partially compensating rather than causing the full drop.

rows.config: diagnostic shared-only-from-dense 2288 for 8x64 top2 discard local-backbone-ft
rows.init: dense checkpoint -> shared-only dense-top-channel 2288, no router, no sparse experts
rows.notes: Eval-only diagnostic matching the 8x64 top2 local experiment. Shared-only 2288 from dense is worse than the trained shared-residual twin by about 0.493 PPL, so the trained residual branch is helping somewhat even though the overall route is still non-competitive.

rows.config: diagnostic shared-only-from-dense 2288 for 8x64 top2 discard moe-only
rows.init: dense checkpoint -> shared-only dense-top-channel 2288, no router, no sparse experts
rows.notes: Eval-only diagnostic matching the 8x64 top2 moe_only experiment. The result again sits well below the trained shared-residual twin, reinforcing that the residual path offers some recovery but far too little to offset the 2288 shared-path compression.

key_conclusions.partition_8e_vs_partition_4e_5k: worse on both 64-batch and 1024-sample evaluation despite healthy routing and strong expert separation
key_conclusions.partition_4e_20k_current_status: substantially improved over partition 4e 5k and close to the non-moe baseline by step 18000, but the run did not finish to 20000 step
key_conclusions.copy_noise_4e_full_top1_5k_takeaway: top-1 active-path-fair full-width routing improves dramatically over top-2 full-width at the same noise setting, but still remains above the non-moe baseline on stable 1024-sample evaluation
key_conclusions.complement_pair_6e_half_top2_5k_takeaway: under the unified reevaluation protocol, the complement-pair design preserves healthy ternary statistics, achieves much stronger specialization than full-copy noise baselines, and is effectively tied with the non-moe baseline: slightly worse at PPL@64 and slightly better at PPL@1024
key_conclusions.relaxed_complement_coverage_5k_takeaway: allowing all 15 top-2 pairs with a fixed coverage penalty does not improve the 6E half-width design at 5K; the model still uses only the three strict complement pairs and ends up slightly worse than the standard aux=0.0001 baseline at PPL@1024
key_conclusions.pair_plus_free_top3_5k_takeaway: adding one free expert on top of the strict complement base pair improves 5K perplexity materially over the standard 6E half-width baseline, but the gain comes from extra active compute at 1.5I and still does not approach the best scratch 20K complement-pair result
key_conclusions.mainline_reeval_20260525_scope: the non-moe baseline and main active-path-fair rows except virtual-group 8e half 20k were refreshed on 2026-05-25 with the current eval protocol; that virtual-group row remains historical because its output directory is unavailable
key_conclusions.continued_finetune_10k_takeaway: continuing from the best aux=0.0001 20K checkpoint with fresh optimizer/scheduler and selective low-lr backbone unfreezing yields only marginal additional gains; partial full fine-tune improves PPL@1024 by about 0.007, while local token-mixer+norm fine-tune is nearly tied with the base 20K checkpoint.
key_conclusions.shared_family_bugfix_scope: full_shared and shared_residual families before 2026-06-03 were contaminated by shared-copy norm/dtype bugs; clean reruns should be used for any structural conclusion.
key_conclusions.full_shared_bugfixed_takeaway: after fixing shared-copy identity, full_shared controls with exact 2816 shared width land essentially on the dense baseline, and 8x32 top2 is the strongest clean variant at 5K.
key_conclusions.shared_residual_topchannel_bugfixed_take: after the same fix, strict-parameter-fair topchannel 2288 + discarded residual reruns remain very weak (~20.06-20.12 PPL@1024), so the old better-looking results were artifacts and the structure itself is the problem.
key_conclusions.shared_only_from_dense_2288_takeaway: eval-only shared-only reconstructions at resolved width 2288 are even worse (~20.55 PPL@1024) than the trained shared_residual counterparts, which means the sparse residual branch partially compensates for shared-width damage rather than causing it.

summary.copy_noise_4e_full_top1_20k_takeaway: training from scratch to 20k substantially improves over the 5k top-1 variant and now very slightly beats the non-moe baseline on both 64-batch and 1024-sample evaluation, but expert similarity remains very high.
summary.complement_pair_6e_half_top2_20k_takeawa: the complement-pair design continues to improve with longer training and now clearly beats the non-moe baseline on both 64-batch and 1024-sample evaluation while preserving moderate specialization and healthy ternary statistics.
summary.complement_pair_6e_half_top2_aux0001_20k: lowering router aux to 0.0001 and training from scratch to 20k yields the strongest complement-pair result so far, improving over the earlier aux=0.005 20k run without harming load balance.
summary.complement_pair_6e_half_top2_aux0001_lay: expanding MoE coverage to layers 6-23 increases parameter count but does not outperform the standard layer12-23 5k configuration, so depth expansion looks lower priority than staying on the 12-layer template.
summary.relaxed_vs_pairfree_5k_takeaway: among the two aggressive routing ablations, relaxed top-2 with coverage penalty fails to unlock new useful paths, while pair-plus-free top-3 is the only one that produces a clear 5K gain; that makes extra active compute look more promising than simply relaxing the pair constraint.
summary.continued_finetune_10k_priority: if continuation-style follow-up is pursued, partial full fine-tune ranks above local token-mixer+norm, but both gains are too small to justify treating continuation as a new mainline over the scratch 20K complement-pair baseline.
summary.random_extreme_local_backbone_40k_takeaw: Both random-extreme local-backbone 40K runs achieve near-zero expert similarity but formal PPL collapses badly, so forcing extreme specialization in this way is counterproductive.
summary.pair_plus_free_scale050_20k_takeaway: Extending pair-plus-free with free_expert_scale=0.50 to 20K keeps routing healthy and improves over 5K variants, but it still does not beat the best strict 6E complement scratch-20K run.
summary.shared_residual_isoarea_5k_takeaway: Both strict-parameter-fair shared-residual iso-area 5K runs are stable and fully evaluable, but neither is competitive: alpha=0.25 is slightly better than alpha=0.10, yet both remain far worse than the non-MoE baseline and current complement-pair mainline.
summary.full_shared_bugfixed_5k_takeaway: With the shared-copy bug fixed and identity verified, exact full-shared 2816 controls return to dense-baseline quality. The 8x32 top2 variants are slightly best, and local_backbone_ft adds only a marginal benefit over moe_only.
summary.shared_residual_topchannel_bugfixed_5k_t: Clean reruns of the 2288 topchannel + discarded residual family remain decisively bad: all four land around 20.06-20.12 PPL@1024. 8x64 top2 is slightly better on PPL than 4x128 top1, but with much worse routing imbalance, so this route is not viable.
summary.shared_only_from_dense_2288_diagnostic_t: The shared-only-from-dense diagnostic at width 2288 is even worse than the trained shared_residual checkpoints by roughly 0.43-0.49 PPL, so sparse residuals are partially recovering lost quality. The primary damage comes from compressing the shared path to 2288, not from adding sparse residuals per se.
